title: Shape Memory Polymers for Active Cell Culture
protocol: Develop a custom curing chamber using a glass slide, Teflon spacer, and aluminum plate held together by binder clips.
Inject NOA63 into the chamber through a hole in the Teflon spacer using an 18 gauge needle.
Heat the NOA63 to ease injection on a hot plate set at 125 °C for 5 min.
Pre-cure the NOA63 in a UV lamp chamber (λmax = 365 nm) for 20 min with the lamp 6.5 cm from the surface of the glass.
Remove the NOA63 from the chamber while warm using a razor blade.
Post-cure the NOA63 under UV light for 3 h 40 m on the hot plate at 125 °C.
Store the NOA63 desiccated at -20 °C.
Prepare a dumbbell specimen by hot-pressing a cured NOA63 film with a customized punch.
Load the specimen into a dynamic mechanical analyzer (DMA) with tensile fixture in "force controlled" mode.
Equilibrate the specimen at 95.00 °C isothermally for 10.00 min.
Ramp force from 0.300 N/min to 2.500 N isothermally for 5.00 min.
Ramp temperature from 2.00 °C/min to 20.00 °C isothermally for 10.00 min.
Ramp force from 0.300 N/min to 0.015 N isothermally for 5.00 min.
Ramp temperature from 2.00 °C/min back to 95.00 °C.
Repeat the previous four steps two more times.
Cut the SMP film with a razor to desired sample size.
Place the SMP on a hot plate set above its Tg temperature to reduce modulus and ease cutting.
Set the temperature of the platens in a bench top hydraulic press above the Tg of the SMP.
Apply a ~100 kPa preload for 5 minutes to allow samples to reach uniform temperature.
Apply 1-6 MPa stress to the samples and hold for 1 minute.
Fracture will occur if larger stresses are applied.
Reduce the temperature below the Tg using water cooling capability of the press platens.
Remove the applied force when the temperature is below the Tg.
Store the samples desiccated at -20°C.
Sterilize the samples with UV light in a biological safety cabinet for 6 h.
Flip the samples to new sterile dishes face up and sterilize again for 6 h.
Place the samples in a 96 well plate and add 150 μl of complete growth medium.
Put the plate in a 30°C incubator with 5% CO2 until reaching the desired partial recovery, typically 30 h.
Place the samples in a new 96 well plate.
Add 150 μl of cell solution to the samples.
Use C3H/10T1/2 mouse embryonic fibroblasts at 20,000 cells/ml to achieve isolated cells.
Place the plate in a 30°C incubator for 9.5 h to allow cell attachment and spreading.
Remove samples for cell morphology assay before transition.
Perform staining and fluorescence imaging on the samples.
Move the plate to a 37 °C incubator for recovery of samples.
Continue culture for 19 hours after moving to the incubator.
Apply appropriate stain (phalloidin for filamentous actin) to the samples.
Proceed with imaging procedures.
Mix NOA63 prepolymer with photoinitiator as supplied by the manufacturer.
Ensure NOA63 allows high cell attachment and viability.
Tune the transition temperature to allow recovery between two cell-compatible temperatures.
Observe that the amplitude of temporary topography (grooves) decreases over time at 30 °C.
Note that by 30 hours at 30 °C, the groove amplitude has reduced by approximately 50%.
Record a further reduction of about 10% in groove amplitude over the next 9.5 hours.
Trigger recovery by increasing temperature to 37 °C.
Measure that the groove amplitude reduces to 0.5% of initial within 9.5 hours at 37 °C.
Confirm that for an embossing stress of 4.9 MPa, a functional change from 13 μm grooves to nearly flat surface occurs.
